description: Expected triage for each issue in papatel5698/calculator-demo's demo/issues.json, keyed by title. Judged against the code at the demo-baseline tag, not only against what each report claims. See docs/decisions/003-answer-key.md.

issues.title: Division by zero crashes the program
issues.reason: The reported crash doesn't reproduce: main() catches every exception, so 10/0 prints the generic "Invalid input". The real defect is the unhelpful message. The expected behaviour ("Error: Division by zero") is spelled out, and the fix is a ZeroDivisionError branch in main() or divide(), with a test. That's small and safe to automate. Medium, not high, because nothing crashes.

issues.title: Empty input crashes the program
issues.reason: Doesn't reproduce. evaluate("") raises ValueError (not the reported IndexError), main() catches it and prints "Invalid input", then re-prompts. That already meets the stated expected behaviour ("show an error message or re-prompt"). Ask the reporter for their version and the traceback before anyone changes code.

issues.title: Division returns integer instead of decimal — 7/2 gives 3
issues.reason: Reproduces: divide() uses // instead of /, so 7/2 gives 3. It's a one-character fix in one function, with an existing xfail test to un-mark. High because it silently returns wrong answers.

issues.title: Whitespace in expressions causes parse error
issues.reason: Reproduces: evaluate() rejects "2 + 3" because operands like "2 " fail the isdigit() check, so the prompt shows "Invalid input". Stripping spaces before tokenising is a small, local fix with an existing xfail test. Medium: users hit it often, but they get an error rather than a wrong answer.

issues.title: Operator precedence is wrong — 2+3*4 returns 20 instead of 14
issues.reason: Reproduces: evaluate() reduces tokens strictly left to right. Fixing it means redesigning the parser (precedence levels, ideally a recursive-descent or shunting-yard parser) and shapes the parentheses feature too. Too much design for an unattended fix. High because it silently returns wrong answers.

issues.title: Add support for parentheses in expressions
issues.reason: New parser capability that depends on how operator precedence gets fixed. Needs a design decision first, so an engineer should own it. Medium: a well-specified, useful feature, but nothing is broken.

issues.title: Add history feature
issues.reason: Too vague to build ("some kind of history... maybe like pressing the up arrow or something?"). It could mean readline-style recall, a history command or saved sessions. Ask what the user wants to do with it. Low until that's clear.

issues.title: It crashed yesterday
issues.reason: No input, steps or error output. The only real crash in the code is a traceback on Ctrl-D or Ctrl-C at the prompt, and there's no way to tell whether that's what happened. Ask what they typed and what they saw.

issues.title: Calculator gives wrong answer for large numbers
issues.reason: No example. Python integers are exact at any size, so +, - and * are correct for large numbers. Division truncates, which is the integer-division bug, but that isn't specific to large numbers. Ask for an input and the expected output.

issues.title: Doesn't work on my machine
issues.reason: No command and no error. The calculator is plain Python with no platform-specific code, so nothing points at Windows. Ask which command they ran and what it printed.

issues.title: Dividing odd numbers gives the wrong answer
issues.reason: Same defect as the integer-division issue, reported in different words: divide() uses //.
issues.duplicate_of: Division returns integer instead of decimal — 7/2 gives 3

issues.title: Can't use spaces when typing a calculation
issues.reason: Same defect as the whitespace issue, reported in different words.
issues.duplicate_of: Whitespace in expressions causes parse error

issues.title: Support brackets like (1+2)*3
issues.reason: Same request as the parentheses issue, in different words.
issues.duplicate_of: Add support for parentheses in expressions

issues.title: Pressing Ctrl-D at the prompt prints a traceback
issues.reason: Reproduces: input() sits outside the try block in main(), so EOFError and KeyboardInterrupt escape as tracebacks. The expected behaviour is stated, and the fix is a small except clause around input() with a test. Medium because users see a crash, even though it only happens when they're leaving.

issues.title: Typing QUIT in capitals doesn't exit
issues.reason: Reproduces: main() compares against ('quit', 'exit') exactly. Lower-casing the input before the check is a one-line fix with a clear expected behaviour. Low: there's an obvious workaround.

issues.title: Negative numbers give Invalid input
issues.reason: Reproduces: the tokeniser treats every '-' as an operator, so '-5' and '3*-2' fail. Unary minus belongs in the parser redesign for precedence; a local patch would have to be redone. Medium: an error on input users normally type.

issues.title: Decimal numbers aren't accepted
issues.reason: Reproduces: the tokeniser uses isdigit() and int(). Supporting decimals changes the number type everywhere and needs design choices: float or Decimal, and how to display 5 versus 5.0 or 0.1+0.2. Medium: a common need.

issues.title: Remove the global result variable from calculator.py
issues.reason: Accurate: the four operations write to a module-level result that nothing reads. Removing the writes changes no behaviour, and the strict-xfail test test_evaluate_leaves_no_module_state proves the fix. Low: no user impact.

issues.title: Remove unused parse_expression()
issues.reason: Accurate: parse_expression() is never called; the only reference is an import in the tests. Delete both. No behaviour change. Low: no user impact.

issues.title: Add type hints and docstrings to calculator.py
issues.reason: Mechanical and behaviour-preserving, with the existing tests as a safety net. Low: no user impact.

issues.title: Add an exponent operator
issues.reason: Needs the parser redesign: exponents bind tighter than * and are right-associative. It also needs a choice of syntax (^ or **). Low: a nice-to-have.

issues.title: Use Python's eval() to fix the parsing bugs
issues.reason: Looks like a safe one-line fix, but it isn't. eval() runs arbitrary Python, so input like __import__('os').system('...') executes commands, and a huge exponent like 9**9**9 hangs the process. It would also make ^ mean XOR. A maintainer should decline it with an explanation; the parsing bugs are tracked in their own issues. Typed as cleanup because it proposes replacing existing code rather than adding behaviour. Low: no defect of its own.

issues.title: Require Python 3.12
issues.reason: A one-line change, but it drops support for everyone on Python 3.9 to 3.11, and nothing in the code needs 3.12. Raising the minimum version is a support-policy decision for the maintainers, not a fix to automate. Low: no defect.
